text:
maya: Heads-up — while investigating the P99 token latency spike on route `chat-beta` I found we don't have a single view tying kernel selection -> batch size -> KV prefix hit behavior together. Can we wire up a short telemetry patch to expose those correlations?

tristan: :+1: We definitely need that. High-level ask: per-request kernel_selected, batch_size_at_dispatch, kv_prefix_hit (bool), kv_eviction_reason, kv_shard_rss_bytes, and token_processing_stage timings (tokenize, forward, kv_lookup, stitch).

maya: Exactly. My proposal: emit a tiny trace tag set per request and aggregate in Prometheus + some histogram buckets. Metric names I sketched: `runtime_kernel_selected{kernel=...,model=...}`, `runtime_batch_size`, `runtime_kv_prefix_reuse_count`, `runtime_kv_evictions_total{reason=...}`, `runtime_kv_shard_rss_bytes`. Also `runtime_token_time_seconds_bucket` with labels stage=(tokenize, forward, kv_lookup, stitch).

ops-bot: Deploy pipeline triggered: ci/runtime-telemetry-wireup. Status: queued.

liam: A couple questions: (1) Do we want to sample full KV key names or only route-tagged prefix hashes? (2) How costly is adding token stage timers at 1kqps?

maya: For privacy and cardinality, sample only a hashed `prefix_tag` derived from (route, prefix_len) — see snippet: ```python
def prefix_tag(route, prefix):
    return sha1(f"{route}:{len(prefix)}")[:8]
```
We should have a 1% full-key sample for debug traces, otherwise just emit `prefix_tag` and `kv_prefix_hit` boolean.

anya: Regarding cost, token-level microtimers are cheap if we use a per-request circular timer pool and only expose aggregated histograms. We did this in 2023 for batching and it added ~0.5% CPU. Still need to validate on T4/T4x.

tristan: Suggest creating a per-route dashboard with these panels:
- Token-level latency waterfall (stacked histograms for tokenize/kv_lookup/forward/stitch)
- Kernel selection heatmap: x=batch_size, y=kernel, color=avg token p50
- KV prefix reuse by route: `kv_prefix_reuse_ratio{route}` time-series + top prefixes table
- Evictions: `increase(runtime_kv_evictions_total[5m])` by reason

maya: I'll draft the PromQL and Grafana panels. Example queries: `sum by(kernel)(rate(runtime_kernel_selected[1m]))` and `histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(runtime_token_time_seconds_bucket{stage="kv_lookup"}[5m])) by (le, route))`. For reuse ratio: `sum(runtime_kv_prefix_reuse_count) by (route) / sum(runtime_kv_prefix_request_total) by (route)`.

liam: Nice. Also add a panel correlating `kernel_selected` with `kv_prefix_reuse_ratio` to see if certain kernels are getting cold cache penalties.

maya: Good call. If we see that kernel A -> low reuse -> higher p99, we may want to bias kernel selection or trigger prefetch for that route.

anya: Operational note: telemetry add will increase metrics cardinality. We must ensure `prefix_tag` is limited and hashed; don't create free-form label for full prefix. Also constrain route label cardinality (we have ~200 routes in prod).

tristan: Action items:
- maya: PR that emits the tags + counts (small native C++ change in runtime dispatcher) — assign to you.
- liam: load test T4 and T4x with telemetry enabled at 100% for 30m and report overhead.
- anya: Grafana dashboard stub + PromQL for panels.
- ops-bot: run canary deploy to alpha.

maya: I'll open the PR today: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pull/7423 (draft). It includes the `prefix_tag` hashing and 1% full-key sampler.

liam: I'll run the perf job after the PR is merged. Quick note — watch for `runtime_kv_shard_rss_bytes` spikes; if shard compaction is running it can look noisy.

tristan: If we get stable signals, next step is an alert: `kv_prefix_reuse_ratio{route} < 0.2` for 10m -> paging oncall with context and top kernel heatmap.

maya: Thanks all. If nobody objects I'll merge draft tomorrow morning and schedule the canary.

anya: No objections from me. :white_check_mark:

ops-bot: Canary deploy started to cluster=alpha, tag=telemetry-wireup-171920. Monitoring channels: #eng-runtime-canary.

tristan: One last thought — include a small profiler label for `batching_strategy` (e.g., adaptive, fixed, static) so we can audit which heuristic correlates with reuse. Label name: `batch_strategy`.

maya: Good idea — will add `batch_strategy` tag (values: adaptive, fixed_window, time_based) to the emitted metrics.

liam: Thanks — will start the perf runs when canary green.

maya: Closing loop, will post follow-up thread with dashboard screenshots and first 24h signals.
